title: The underived exchange morphism is linear on sheaves of modules
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square],
$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
 f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
 Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y,
 \end{array}
$$
let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and, for a scheme $T$, let $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the category of sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $u\in\{f,f',g,g'\}$ let $u^{-1}:\Mod(\mathrm{target}_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(\mathrm{source}_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the inverse image of sheaves of modules and $u_*$ the direct image of sheaves of modules, $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; on underlying abelian sheaves they are the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] of abelian sheaves. For $G\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ let $\Ex^0_{\square,G}:g^{-1}f_*G\to f'_*g'^{-1}G$ be the underived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] of the underlying abelian sheaf of $G$. Then $\Ex^0_{\square,G}$ is $\Lambda_{Y'}$-linear for the module structures of $g^{-1}f_*G$ and $f'_*g'^{-1}G$ given by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], i.e. it is a morphism of $\Mod(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Consequently the morphisms $\Ex^0_{\square,G}$, $G\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, form a natural transformation $\Ex^0_\square:g^{-1}\circ f_*\to f'_*\circ g'^{-1}$ of functors $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$ whose underlying morphisms of abelian sheaves are the abelian underived exchange morphisms. (This is what makes the exchange of Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), available ``on sheaves of modules''.)

proof.text: *The square isomorphism is linear.* By [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] the specified isomorphism of the square is $\theta_\square=c_{f,g'}^{-1}\circ c_{g,f'}:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(g\circ f')^{-1}=(f\circ g')^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}$, with the composition isomorphisms $c$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2) (this is the definition of the source Lean `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.squareUpperStarIso`: both composites are identified with the inverse image along the one morphism $g\circ f'=f\circ g':X'\to Y$). Let $M\in\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Since $g\circ f'=f\circ g'$ is one morphism, $(g\circ f')^{-1}M=(f\circ g')^{-1}M$ as sheaves of $\Lambda_{X'}$-modules [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] (2), $c_{g,f',M}:f'^{-1}g^{-1}M\to(g f')^{-1}M$ and $c_{f,g',M}:g'^{-1}f^{-1}M\to(f g')^{-1}M$ are $\Lambda_{X'}$-linear isomorphisms. The inverse of a linear isomorphism of sheaves of modules is linear (its components are inverses of bijective $\Lambda_{X'}(W)$-linear maps, and they commute with restrictions because the original components do) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Hence $\theta_{\square,M}$ is $\Lambda_{X'}$-linear for every $M\in\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

proof.text: *The adjoint of $\Ex^0$ is linear.* Let $G\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2), (3), $f_*G\in\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $g^{-1}f_*G$ and $f'^{-1}g^{-1}f_*G$, $f^{-1}f_*G$, $g'^{-1}f^{-1}f_*G$ and $g'^{-1}G$ are sheaves of modules whose underlying abelian sheaves are the abelian images, and the module functors $u^{-1}$, $u_*$ act on morphisms as the abelian ones. By (3) of that proposition the counit $\varepsilon_{f,G}:f^{-1}f_*G\to G$ of the abelian adjunction is the counit of the module adjunction, hence $\Lambda_X$-linear; by (2), $g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,G}$ is the module inverse image of a linear morphism, hence $\Lambda_{X'}$-linear. By step 1 with $M=f_*G$, $\theta_{\square,f_*G}$ is $\Lambda_{X'}$-linear. So the composite $\varphi_G=g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,G}\circ\theta_{\square,f_*G}:f'^{-1}(g^{-1}f_*G)\to g'^{-1}G$ of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is a morphism of $\Mod(X'_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

proof.text: *$\Ex^0_{\square,G}$ is linear.* By [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], $\Ex^0_{\square,G}:g^{-1}f_*G\to f'_*g'^{-1}G$ is the adjoint of $\varphi_G$ under the abelian adjunction $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$, i.e. $\Ex^0_{\square,G}=f'_*(\varphi_G)\circ\eta_{f',g^{-1}f_*G}$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (3) (with $u=f'$, the sheaf of modules $g^{-1}f_*G$ on $Y'_{\Et}$ and the sheaf of modules $g'^{-1}G$ on $X'_{\Et}$), the abelian adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ab}(f'^{-1}g^{-1}f_*G,g'^{-1}G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ab}(g^{-1}f_*G,f'_*g'^{-1}G)$ restricts to the bijection between $\Lambda_{X'}$-linear and $\Lambda_{Y'}$-linear morphisms (the unit $\eta_{f'}$ is linear and $f'_*$ of a linear morphism is linear). Since $\varphi_G$ is $\Lambda_{X'}$-linear (step 2), $\Ex^0_{\square,G}$ is $\Lambda_{Y'}$-linear for the module structures of $g^{-1}f_*G$ and $f'_*g'^{-1}G$ given by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], i.e. a morphism of $\Mod(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

proof.text: *Naturality.* Let $a:G\to G'$ be a morphism of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. The module functors $g^{-1}\circ f_*$ and $f'_*\circ g'^{-1}$ send $a$ to the abelian morphisms $g^{-1}f_*a$ and $f'_*g'^{-1}a$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2), (3), and by [lemma-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-naturality] $f'_*g'^{-1}a\circ\Ex^0_{\square,G}=\Ex^0_{\square,G'}\circ g^{-1}f_*a$ as morphisms of abelian sheaves. Composition in $\Mod(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$ is composition of the underlying morphisms of abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so the same equality holds in $\Mod(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$, all four morphisms being linear (step 3). Hence the $\Ex^0_{\square,G}$ form a natural transformation $\Ex^0_\square:g^{-1}\circ f_*\to f'_*\circ g'^{-1}$ of functors $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$ whose underlying morphisms are the abelian underived exchange morphisms.
